does: Cooks filled, rolled leaves packed snugly seam down in a lined pot, weighed down with a plate, in a little oil, lemon juice and water. The leaves turn soft and tart and the rice inside swells and softens.

intro.what: Filled leaves simmer gently while packed snugly in a lined pot.
intro.why: It teaches you to support delicate rolls and manage liquid as the filling swells.

how: Line the base of a wide pot with slices of tomato or a few spare leaves, so that the rolls do not catch.
Pack the rolls tightly, seam down, in circles, layer on layer, so that none can unroll.
Pour in the olive oil and the lemon juice, add water to come part of the way up the rolls, and salt the liquid.
Set a plate that fits inside the pot upside down on the rolls, so that they stay put.
Cover, bring to a gentle simmer and cook on a low heat until the leaves are tender and the filling has swelled. Leave the rolls to cool in the pot.

cues.text: The rolls are plump and have kept their shape, and the liquid is mostly taken up and glossy with oil.
A leaf is tender and the rice inside is soft when a roll is pressed.

mistakes.mistake: Packing the rolls loosely, so that they float and unroll.
mistakes.fix: Pack them tight and weigh them with a plate.

mistakes.mistake: Covering the rolls completely with liquid, so that the filling washes out and the dish turns watery.
mistakes.fix: Add liquid only part of the way up.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking on a high heat, which splits the leaves and breaks the rolls.
mistakes.fix: Keep the pot at a gentle simmer.

quiz.question: Why pack the rolls snugly and weigh them with a plate?
choices: To keep them from floating and unrolling.
To press the filling out into the liquid.
To expose each seam to stronger bubbling.
quiz.because: Support from neighbouring rolls and the plate helps the wrappers stay closed.

quiz.question: Why line the pot base with spare leaves or tomato?
choices: To increase direct contact with the hot metal.
To keep the rolls from catching on the base.
quiz.because: A lining separates delicate wrappers from the pot surface.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the intended result?
choices: Split wrappers floating in a watery pot.
Loose filling washed out between leaves.
Plump intact rolls with mostly absorbed liquid.
quiz.because: The filling swells while the supported wrappers retain their shapes.

quiz.question: The wrappers split during vigorous cooking. What would you change next time?
choices: Keep the liquid at a gentle simmer.
Maintain the boil and stir the rolls.
Remove the plate and increase bubbling.
quiz.because: Gentler liquid movement reduces stress on the delicate leaves.

comes_after.why: The leaves are filled and rolled first, and a loose roll will not survive the pot.

variant_of.differs: The food is rolled leaves packed seam down and held under a plate, in liquid that comes only part of the way up, and it is left to cool in the pot.
